reason: This passage (1 Samuel 25) describes a private dispute between David and Nabal, a wealthy individual who disrespectfully rejects David's messengers, followed by Abigail's intervention to prevent bloodshed. While Nabal shows disrespect to David as an individual, this does not constitute the Hebrew people complaining about their leaders. The narrative focuses entirely on personal/interpersonal conflicts and contains no depiction of the nation or general population voicing complaints about Samuel, David, Saul, or any other national leaders.
